events.title: The Pazzi conspiracy
events.shortBlurb: At High Mass in Florence's cathedral, daggers fell upon the Medici brothers…
body: On Sunday, 26 April 1478, at High Mass in Florence's cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, the conspirators of the Pazzi family struck: Giuliano de' Medici was stabbed to death on the cathedral floor — nineteen wounds, the record runs — while his brother Lorenzo, wounded, beat back his attackers and escaped into the sacristy.

The plot had been woven around Girolamo Riario, nephew of Pope Sixtus IV, with Francesco Salviati, archbishop of Pisa, and the Pazzi, papal bankers and rivals of the Medici; the king of Naples was privy to it, and the tradition relates that the blow was timed for the elevation of the Host, when heads would be bowed. But the city rose for the Medici: the archbishop was hanged from the windows of the Signoria in his very cassock, and Jacopo de' Pazzi was put to death within days.

Sixtus IV answered with an interdict on Florence and the excommunication of Lorenzo, and war followed with Naples, until Lorenzo's bold journey to King Ferrante in the winter of 1479–80 made the peace. The sacrilege at the altar shocked even a violent age, and the Pazzi name became a byword for treachery.
